title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. Grothendieck is building the combinatorial skeleton of the boundary ('structure à l'infini') of the moduli stack of stable ν-pointed genus-g curves, written M̄_{g,ν}. An 'MD-graphe', soon renamed 'maquette', is the marked dual graph of a stable curve. It has vertices α of genus g_α, edges (the nodes), and legs (the marked points I). Two relations hold: g = Σ g_α + h_1, and s_0 − s_1 = h_0 − h_1 = 1 for a connected graph. Stability means every genus-0 vertex has total valence (edges plus legs) at least 3.

The previous page proves the Proposition that the type (g,ν) of such a graph is 'anabelian', i.e. 2g + ν ≥ 3. It first excludes (g,ν) = (1,0).

First part of this page: the case g = 0, ν ≤ 2.
- From 0 = Σ g_α + h_1, every g_α = 0 and h_1 = 0, so the graph is a tree with all vertices of genus 0.
- It cannot be a single vertex: that would be a smooth stable (0,ν)-curve with ν ≤ 2, which does not exist.
- So the tree has at least two leaves ('bouts').
- A genus-0 leaf has exactly one edge, so it must carry at least 2 marked points.
- Hence ν ≥ 2 + 2 = 4, contradicting ν ≤ 2.
The argument is complete and correct.

Second part: definitions.
- G is a maquette (marked stable graph).
- A standard (stable marked) curve C over an algebraically closed field is 'of type G' if its maquette (dual marked graph) is isomorphic to G.
- It is 'G-épinglée' (G-rigidified) if an isomorphism maquette(C) ≅ G is given. This extra structure is called a G-épinglage.
- Over an arbitrary base S, a standard curve (X̂, I) is of type G if all its geometric fibres are of type G.

The next page continues: the fibrewise maquettes then form a 'schéma en maquettes' over S. This is a system of finite étale covers of S (vertices, half-edges with involution, marked points) together with maps between them, étale-locally isomorphic to the constant G_S. G-épinglages are the sections of a torsor under Γ_S, where Γ = Aut G is finite. This is the setup for describing the boundary stratum indexed by G as (∏_α M_{g_α, ν̂_α})/Aut G, where ν̂_α counts legs plus half-edges at α.

In modern terms: the boundary stratification of M̄_{g,n} by stable graphs, the monodromy action of π_1 of a stratum on the dual graph, and the rigidified Aut(G)-torsor over the stratum.
errors: No mathematical error. The step 'cannot be reduced to a single vertex' tacitly uses that a one-vertex graph of type (0,ν) with ν ≤ 2 is not stable. This parallels the explicit remark on the previous page.

ideas.what: Stable marked graphs exist only for 2g+ν ≥ 3; the case g=0, ν≤2 is excluded via leaves of a tree each needing ≥2 legs
ideas.modern_name: Stable graphs / non-existence of unstable types; leaf counting for stable trees

ideas.what: Curves of type G and G-épinglage (choice of an isomorphism of the dual graph with a fixed graph G); over a base, the dual graph as an étale-locally constant 'scheme of maquettes', with rigidifications forming an Aut(G)-torsor
ideas.modern_name: Boundary stratification of M̄_{g,n} by stable graphs; G-marked stable curves; monodromy on dual graphs; M_G = (∏ M_{g_v,n_v})/Aut G
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford 1969, Knudsen 1983; graph formalism by Kontsevich–Manin 1994, Getzler–Kapranov 1998; systematic treatment in Arbarello–Cornalba–Griffiths (2011) and Graber–Pandharipande
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the 'structure à l'infini' and the boundary of M̄_{g,ν} in outline only

deep.surprise_reason: Routine combinatorial verification plus standard definitions of graph-type strata and graph rigidifications. These are all well established in the later literature. Only the terminology ('maquette', 'G-épinglage') is idiosyncratic.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Elimin[ons] [?] [le] cas' is probably 'Éliminons de même le cas g=0, ν≤2. Ici ...'; the second 'Je' is likely 'Il' ('Il ne peut être réduit à un seul sommet').
'h' in 'Σ g_a + h' is h_1 (first Betti number), as on the previous page.
'Soit G un [-MD-] [-graphe-] {+marqué [?]+}' should read 'Soit G une maquette' ('maquette' is written above, replacing 'MD-graphe').
'une [-MD-] courbe [-stable-] {+stable+}' should read 'une courbe standard': 'standard' is written above the crossed-out 'stable'.
'si sa marquée [?] est iso à G' / 'un iso entre sa marquée [?] et G' should read 'sa maquette'.
'ses fibres géom. {+marquées+}' is likely 'ses fibres géom. sont du type G'; the inserted word above is 'maquettes', belonging to the final line 'Alors les maquettes des [fibres géom.]'.
'Soit (X̂, I) une courbe stable sur une base S' is likely 'courbe standard'.
